title: Multiplying and Dividing Integers
seo_title: Grade 7 Multiplying and Dividing Integers Worksheets: Sign Rules, Fractions and Word Problems
standard_text: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication and division and of fractions to multiply and divide rational numbers.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 multiplying and dividing integers worksheets: the sign rules, many factors and powers of negatives, decimals and fractions, and real-world word problems. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: Same signs give a positive. Different signs give a negative.
key_sub: (−6) × (−4) = 24 and −56 ÷ 8 = −7. With many factors, count the negatives: even is positive, odd is negative.
body_html:
The sign rules

Multiply or divide the sizes as usual. Then choose the sign: same signs give a positive, different signs give a negative. Division uses the same rules, because division undoes multiplication.

SignsAnswerExample
positive × positive+4 × 3 = 12
negative × negative+(−4) × (−3) = 12
positive × negative−4 × (−3) = −12
negative × positive−(−4) × 3 = −12

Why is negative × negative positive?

Look at the pattern: (−4) × 2 = −8, (−4) × 1 = −4, (−4) × 0 = 0. Each step the answer goes up by 4. So (−4) × (−1) = 4 and (−4) × (−2) = 8.

Many factors

Count the negative factors. An even number of negatives gives a positive. An odd number gives a negative. (−2)3 = (−2)(−2)(−2) = −8.

Example

Find −56 ÷ (−8).

Different or same? Both are negative, so the answer is positive.

56 ÷ 8 = 7.

Answer: 7

Example

Find −34 ÷ 12.

Multiply by the reciprocal: −34 × 21.

Different signs, so the answer is negative: −64 = −1 12.

Answer: −1 12

You can move the negative sign: −(p ÷ q) = (−p) ÷ q = p ÷ (−q). Dividing by 0 is undefined.

Common mistakes

  • Using the adding rule: (−6) × (−4) is 24, not −24 or −10.
  • Counting negatives wrongly: (−1)(−2)(−3) has three negatives, so it is −6.
  • Forgetting to flip when dividing fractions: −34 ÷ 12 is −1 12, not −38.

faq.q: What are the rules for multiplying integers?
faq.a: Multiply the sizes. If the two signs are the same, the answer is positive: (−6) × (−4) = 24. If they are different, the answer is negative: 6 × (−4) = −24.

faq.q: Are the division rules the same?
faq.a: Yes. Same signs give a positive and different signs give a negative: −56 ÷ (−8) = 7 and −56 ÷ 8 = −7.

faq.q: Why is a negative times a negative positive?
faq.a: Follow the pattern (−4) × 2 = −8, (−4) × 1 = −4, (−4) × 0 = 0. The answer goes up by 4 each time, so (−4) × (−1) = 4.

faq.q: How do I find the sign with many factors?
faq.a: Count the negative factors. An even count gives a positive answer and an odd count gives a negative answer. If any factor is 0, the product is 0.

items.q: A quotient of two integers is negative. What must be true?
items.e: A quotient is negative only when one number is positive and the other is negative.
